newsitem.title: USA: SEC clears Denver in airport muni bond probe - city.
newsitem.headline: SEC clears Denver in airport muni bond probe - city.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has notified the city of Denver that it has been cleared of charges in the commission's probe of Denver International Airport bonds, a spokesman for Denver Mayor Wellington Webb said on Friday.

"The city of Denver has received official confirmation from the SEC that it has been cleared in an investigation of municipal bond fraud regarding construction (of) the Denver International Airport," Webb spokesman Andrew Hudson told Reuters in telephone interview.
He said the city will hold a press briefing shortly.

The SEC's Denver office had informed the city last October that it planned to urge commissioners to bring an "administrative action" against the city for violating the antifraud provisions of the federal securities laws.

SEC's Denver staff said the city failed to disclose to bond investors potential problems with a state-of-the-art baggage handling system that led to a 16-month delay in opening the $4.9 billion facility and mushrooming costs.
The city disputed the staff charges in a 20-page letter on December 7, claiming Congress did not intend federal securities fraud charges to apply to state and local issuers.
The SEC's letter to Denver says: "This is to inform you that the present staff inquiry has been terminated and that, at this time, no enforcement action has been recommended to the Commission.

"It's a proper result and I think its a good indication that the Wells process of the SEC works," Thomas Boyle, attorney for Denver said. He was referring to the SEC staff procedure of notifying potential defendents of a pending enforcement action and seeking their input.
"Obviously, we're pleased," said Daniel Muse, Denver city attorney. "After two years the SEC has determined there is no basis" for action, he said.
